messages.author: e7a71d967e60bb41
messages.subject: Plotting Multiple Lines and Legend
parts:
Dear All,
Maybe the answer to this is a one-liner, but I need some help.
Consider the snippet at the end of the email.
The result is definitely not what I would like to achieve.
I would like to plot ml1, ml2 and ml3 as three separate lines, but ml1
and ml3 should have the same color and have the same description in the
legend.
My problem is that ml1 and ml2 get mixed up in the plot.
How can I solve that?
My original problem amounts to plotting hundreds of lines with only a
few colors (predefined groups of different lines should have the same
color), so I end up with an object like ml_tmp, hence (in the case of my
example) I would like a fix which relies on ml_tmp to plot three
distinct lines with two colors and only 2 corresponding entries in the
legend.
Can anyone help me out with this?
Many thanks

Lorenzo


####################################################
####################################################
####################################################

library(ggplot2)
library(Cairo)


ml1 <- cbind(seq(10),seq(10))
ml1 <- as.data.frame(ml1)

ml2 <- cbind(seq(20),2*seq(20))
ml2 <- as.data.frame(ml2)

ml3 <- cbind(seq(30),3*seq(30))
ml3 <- as.data.frame(ml3)

names(ml1) <- c("time","my_function")
names(ml2) <- c("time","my_function")
names(ml3) <- c("time","my_function")


ml_tmp <- rbind(transform(ml1, set="Aggregated"),
transform(ml2, set="30 Rewirings"), transform(ml3,
set="Aggregated"))


gpl <- ggplot(ml_tmp, aes(x=time, y=my_function, colour=set, shape=set)) +
geom_line(size=0.5)

CairoPDF("Test_legend.odf")
print(gpl)
dev.off()

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Plotting Multiple Lines and Legend
parts:
Hi Lorenzo:

Does this do what you want? I think all you need to add is a data set indicator...

ml1 <- cbind(seq(10),seq(10))
ml2 <- cbind(seq(20),2*seq(20))
ml3 <- cbind(seq(30),3*seq(30))
 ml <- as.data.frame(rbind(ml1, ml2, ml3))
> names(ml)
[1] "V1" "V2"
> dim(ml)
[1] 60  2
# data set indicator
ml$ds <- factor(rep(1:3, c(10, 20, 30)))
# factor on which to map color
ml$set <- factor(rep(c('Aggregated', '30 Rewirings', 'Aggregated'),
                      c(10, 20, 30))
# Use ds to influence shape of points, set to influence color
p1 <- ggplot(ml, aes(x = V1, y = V2, shape = ds, colour = set))
p1 + geom_point(size = 0.5) + geom_line()

To get rid of the shape legend, add scale_shape(legend = FALSE).

HTH,
Dennis

Thanks for your help. Your suggestion is what I am looking for. However,
I am experiencing some problems when the number of levels grows.
See the snippet at the end of the email (based on yours). I have 20
lines (hence 20 datasets) that I want to plot using 10 colors.
I believe I have simply expanded your example, but when I run it, this
is what I get

Error: scale_shape_discrete can deal with a maximum of 6 discrete
values, but you have 20. See ?scale_manual for a possible alternative

but my attempts with scale_shape_manual have not been successful. I
actually want to plot only lines, not points, but removing shape = ds
from the aesthetics specifications does not get the job done (the
straight lines get wriggled).
Any help is really appreciated.
Cheers

Lorenzo
##############################################################
##############################################################
##############################################################

library(ggplot2)
library(Cairo)

n_seq <- 20

x_seq <- rep(seq(20),n_seq)

y_seq <- c()
my_factor <- c()
set_ind <- c()

for (i in seq(n_seq)){
j <- floor(i/2)+1
y_seq <- c(y_seq,i*seq(20))
my_factor <- c(my_factor,rep(j,n_seq))
set_ind <- c(set_ind,rep(i,20))
}

my_factor[which(my_factor==11)] <- 10

t_lab <- c("a","b","c","d","e","f","g","h","i","l")
## my_factor <- (rep(1:10, 2*n_seq))

ml <- cbind(as.data.frame(x_seq),as.data.frame(y_seq))
names(ml) <- c("x_t","y_t")
#data set indicator
ml$ds <- factor(set_ind)
## # factor on which to map color
ml$set <- factor(t_lab[my_factor])
## # Use ds to influence shape of points, set to influence color
p1 <- ggplot(ml, aes(x = x_t, y = y_t, shape = ds, colour = set))+
# geom_point(size = 0.5) + geom_line()
geom_line()+
scale_shape(legend = FALSE) #to get rid of the shape legend

CairoPDF("Test_legend2.pdf")
print(p1)
dev.off()
